chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: Arranging for Woody Herman's band
summary: He travelled with the band, rehearsed his own charts including Peace Brother and Pick-a-Rib, and wrote the jazz numbers while others did sweet tunes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What were some of the arrangements you did for Woody's band?
"Peace, Brother and "Pick-a-Rib", "Say Si Si" and "After You're Gone", and "Woody Chops Wood", and so on, like that.
"Three Ways To Smoke A Pipe?" That was one of Woody's --
No, I didn't do that. No, no, I didn't= do that one.
Did you travel with the band, or did you just stay home and write and send him the arrangements?
No, I travelled with the band. But, see, the band would go on location and I'd be right there.
Would you rehearse the band for your arrangements?
Oh, yes, yes. I would rehearse the band. Each arranger -- I was on the staff. Each arranger would rehearse his arrangements.
How many arrangements did he have there?

Joe Bishop, he was the -- and Yoder was the bass man, he would make arrangements. Joe Bishop was the flugelhorn man, and he made arrangements. Now, the ones that didn't play was Jiggs Noble Gigs Tuber, and myself. Yes. They had -- most of those boys did the sweet tunes, and you know what I had to do? I had to do the rip-and-farin (unintelligible). I had to do the jazz tunes for them.
